parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a federal document/entry regime (X markers halted; officers instructed to refuse cases where 'reasonable doubt' about sex exists; fraud findings threatened) with roughly 21 states barring congruent facility use (4 with criminal triggers) and division-level hostility. Documented traveller-facing harms are severe: a 2025 bathroom arrest with men's-ward holding; an August 2026 mob assault where victims were charged, attackers not arrested, one denied hospital care and jailed/searched by a male guard despite a female marker; federal custody conversion-therapy policy; abuse in immigration custody. Mitigation is real but partial: functioning courts (several orders enjoined), a national hate-crime statute, ongoing litigation, and 29 states plus the capital with no facility ban. No identity criminalisation, no execution pathway.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable tells officers to refuse any case with document discrepancy or 'reasonable doubt' about sex; X-marker passports halted; possible fraud finding risking lifetime ineligibility; travellers report passports blocked/confiscated, some stranded; eight-plus governments issued travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, with limited waivers; challenge pending in national courts; legal-aid FAQ maintained.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal or fraud suspicion can escalate into immigration custody, where trans detainees document beatings, forced labour and sexual abuse.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans woman arrested 19 Mar 2025 under bathroom trespass law, held 24h in men's ward; Aug 2026 assault victim jailed in men's facility and searched by a male guard despite female licence marker; federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (hair, hormones, drugs) from 2026.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass offence requires willful entry plus refusal to leave, not automatic arrest; national hate-crime statute; litigation active; no identity-based criminalisation as such.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document marker did not determine housing or search in custody — birth-sex placement overrides presentation and papers once detained.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities; 9+1 states cover all government buildings, 9 more schools plus some buildings, 3 schools-only, 6 reaching private settings; 4 states criminalise in some circumstances; one municipality passed an ordinance called among the country's most severe.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states, 4 units and the capital district have no such ban in mapped categories; statutory exemptions listed; trespass trigger requires refusal to depart.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor entering government buildings, schools, parks or courthouses in banning states faces universal exclusion exposure regardless of personal conduct.

care_services.exposure: Aug 2026 assault victim denied hospital care before being taken to jail; gender-affirming care for minors banned in 27 states, affecting a travelling trans minor; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 patient records; proposed federal rules bar public-insurance reimbursement for trans under-18s.
care_services.protection: Several executive orders and rules blocked or enjoined in court; some states retain care access; national employment-discrimination ruling stands.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking can expose identity to records scrutiny; a minor's emergency or routine need collides with state bans the visitor cannot shop around in an emergency.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; executive orders call care 'mutilation' and direct investigation of schools; 2025 poll: 66% back birth-sex listing on documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo states the reward never uses that phrase as a criterion; strategy says powers won't target mere disagreement; marriage equality and national employment protection remain.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises outing probability and emboldens private hostility, while the enforcement carve-outs keep it from being formally operative against individuals.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care banned for minors in 27 states; executive order directs criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; school and facility exclusion rules apply to a visiting minor; hospital-record subpoenas target under-19s.
minors_guardians.protection: Orders partially enjoined; several states retain protective policy; prosecution provision targets school staff, not visiting parents — parent liability not documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family's exposure moves from school/facility exclusion to care denial to, in the worst case, investigation once records are subpoenaed.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Aug 2026 mob beat a trans couple over restroom use; both victims charged with disturbing the peace, no attacker arrested, plea deal unsigned; a 2024 prison killing of a trans inmate; division sits in the lowest equality band. Killing-rate figure is an undercount floor and cannot be used as magnitude.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National 2009 hate-crime statute supplies federal prosecution where the division's 1997 statute omits gender identity; 23 states cover gender identity in bias laws; incident prompted hostile press coverage.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local impunity pushes recourse to federal prosecution, whose reliability here is contested by simultaneous federal hostility.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No division law barring gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing or public accommodations; 1997 bias statute excludes gender identity; unenforceable sodomy statute retained; most federal measures are in litigation, so operative rules shift by travel date.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts have enjoined several orders; pending ACLU-style suit on passport markers; national hate-crime and employment protections; legal-aid FAQ tracks document rules.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist but are slow and uncertain while rules are actively litigated, and the division-level hostility is largely unremedied locally.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars every visibly trans visitor outright with appeals that never succeed. Here refusal is triggered by document discrepancy or 'reasonable doubt' rather than status alone, waivers and litigation exist, and 29 states impose no facility ban. Lower probability and less total exclusion, but comparable administrative reach at the border; ours rates higher.

Vesskar shows routine checkpoint exposure, a deceptive-presentation public-order statute, documented detention, thin legal aid and inconsistent districts — very close to this dossier's entry and facility profile. This dossier adds a recent mob assault with victims charged, no attackers arrested, and birth-sex custody search/denied care, so it sits slightly lower.

Kestrel Isles offers secondary screening, discretionary refusal and slow appeals, but no documented custody abuse, birth-sex imprisonment placement, or state-tolerated street violence. Those added tiers of severity place this dossier materially below 0.55.

Ostravia combines birth-sex prison housing, criminalised cross-dressing in public buildings and slow remedies with no documented impunity pattern. This dossier has comparable custody exposure but functioning federal courts, a national hate-crime statute and large protective regions, so it sits above this anchor.

parsed.synthesis: Traveller exposure runs through three linked stages. At entry, the sex-doubt refusal rule and halted marker flexibility create a universal screening exposure whose escalation path — fraud finding, immigration custody — reaches documented abuse. Inside, federal and 21-plus state facility bans exclude the outed visitor from government buildings, with criminal trespass triggers in four states and a 2025 arrest proving enforcement. In the division, the operative regime is worst: a 2026 mob assault produced charges against the victims, no attacker arrests, denied hospital care, and male-guard search in a men's jail regardless of document marker — state response is itself the exposure, with local remedy absent. Recourse is real but external: federal hate-crime law, enjoining courts, and pending litigation. Net: no criminalisation of identity, functioning institutions partially working for trans people, yet documented universal exclusions, custody harm and impunity place it in Elevated Risk.
